prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Across the five frames, the map places the closet contents in frames 1–2 very near the camera wearer, roughly 0.2–1 m away, while the bed, walls, and windows lie farther away at about 1.5–4 m; in frames 3–5, the bright nearby figure is approximately 0.5–1.5 m away and the room surfaces recede behind them. It clarifies depth ordering that is ambiguous in RGB: hanging garments occlude the room at first, then retreat left and out of view as the camera turns right, revealing a person in front of the camera, the bed to the right, and windows or wall surfaces behind and to the left. The person moves from the right side of frame 2 to near the centre-right in frames 3–4, remaining closer than the bed, while the final view places the bed on the right at roughly 1–2.5 m and the far wall beyond it; only the closest clothes and person appear within the camera wearer's arm's reach. Absolute distances are uncertain because this is monocular depth, and broad halos, missing edges, and inconsistent brightness on the bed, windows, and person make fine spacing and inter-object distances unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map identifies several foreground regions in frames 1–2 as people and ties, but the RGB shows that many of these are hanging clothes about 0.2–1 m from the camera, so those class labels are unreliable even though the masks correctly show strong foreground occlusion of the room. In frames 2–4 it more plausibly isolates one person, initially on the right and then near centre-right, approximately 0.5–1.5 m from the camera, with a bed to that person's right or partly behind them and small potted plants farther left or right at roughly 1.5–3 m. The masks make object boundaries and overlap clearer than RGB: the person partly blocks the bed and window area, the plants occupy small lower or side regions, and several objects are clipped by frame edges as the camera turns from the closet toward the windows and bed. The map does not reliably establish facing direction, gaze, metric distance, or whether objects are within another person's reach, and it appears to merge, omit, or mislabel large portions of the bed, clothing, plants, and background—especially in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects a single small body skeleton only in frame 4, positioned around centre-right where the RGB shows the nearby person; no body or hand skeleton is recovered in frames 1–3 or 5. The detected joints suggest an upright person about 0.5–1.5 m in front of the camera wearer, with the head above the torso and arms extending slightly to the sides, but the sparse two-dimensional skeleton does not securely determine whether the person faces or looks toward the camera. Relative to the RGB, it makes approximate limb placement visible despite the dark clothing and background, while the lack of magenta hand detections means hand position, reach, and contact with the bed, window, or plants cannot be established. The skeleton's distorted proportions and missing lower-body detail, together with complete detection failures in the other frames, make motion, turning, occlusion, and approach or retreat unreliable to infer from this map alone.
